references.text: An eternal statute prohibiting the eating of fat and blood, which applies to all generations of the children of Israel.
The consequence of eating fat from animals sacrificed to the Lord: that person shall be cut off from their people.
Description of how the fat from the sin offering is to be handled—it belongs to the Lord and must be burned on the altar.
The fat is to be burned as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, which explains why the Israelites were not to eat it.
List of clean animals that may be eaten, including ox, sheep, and goat—the same animals mentioned in Leviticus 7:23.
Abel offered the firstborn of his flock and their fat, showing that the fat was regarded as the best part and belonged to God.
